requirements.requirement: node4 runs a persistent HTTP service on TCP port 8080
requirements.summary: A systemd-managed python3 http.server was started and enabled on node4:8080, verified active and answering locally and remotely before and after the node4 restart.

requirements.requirement: Service is published on TCP port 80 of node2's transit address
requirements.summary: A DNAT/port-forward (pf rdr) rule on node2 maps transit interface tcp/80 to 10.10.14.2:8080, with a matching pass rule; curls to http://10.10.12.2:80/ from node1 and node3 return node4's content both before and after node2's restart.

requirements.requirement: node1 has a route to node2's transit address
requirements.summary: node1's eth1 is configured (persistently, via VyOS configure/commit/save) with 10.10.12.1/24, directly connected to node2's transit address 10.10.12.2, and the successful curl through node1's forwarding path confirms reachability; ip_forward is enabled.

requirements.requirement: node3 on lan-a reaches the service by asking node2 rather than addressing node4 directly
requirements.summary: node3 was given a persistent route to 10.10.12.0/24 via node1; curl to node2's transit address (10.10.12.2:80) succeeds and returns node4's content repeatedly, including after all four restarts, while a direct curl attempt to node4 (10.10.14.2:8080) times out because node3 has no route to lan-b and falls back to the unrelated control-plane default route.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly satisfied: node4's HTTP service is published via a DNAT rule on node2's transit address at port 80, node1 has a direct route/adjacency to that address with forwarding enabled, and node3 was demonstrated (via curl and a failed direct attempt to node4) to reach the service only by addressing node2. The executor additionally ran the full node-restart evidence protocol on all four nodes, capturing pre-restart healthy baselines, reboot acknowledgements, changed boot identities, and post-restart recovery of addressing, routes, NAT rules, and the working end-to-end curl path for each node — this is not a task requirement but strengthens confidence in the persistence of the solution.
limitations: The claim that node1 has 'a route' to node2's transit address rests on the two being directly connected on the same /24 rather than an explicit static route entry; this is an equally valid competent implementation given the topology, not a gap.

Some intermediate diagnostic mutations (interface address swaps, temporary ICMP pass rules) were not individually traced end-to-end for removal beyond the final grep-based check on node2; the after-executor lifecycle snapshot corroborates no residual artifacts but does not exhaustively enumerate every intermediate pf rule.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map directly to legitimate prerequisites (interface addressing, DNAT/route configuration, service creation) or to bounded final evidence collection. Several exploratory mutations occurred during initial topology discovery: node1's eth1 was temporarily flushed and reassigned to the wrong subnet (10.10.14.1) while probing physical adjacency, then flushed back to the correct 10.10.12.1/24 (cmd-6bd4b607c25a4685, cmd-c6f27d0e15ad4d31, reverted by cmd-8e2e5f71ecbf431c); node2's vtnet1/vtnet2 addresses were likewise swapped and swapped back during the same probing (cmd-9e5d3ab7718a4b45, corrected by cmd-b021b18c0ceb4d17). Temporary 'antrieb: temp allow icmp for topology probe' pf rules were added to node2 during discovery (visible in cmd-432588fc2eaa4247) and confirmed absent from the final restored configuration (cmd-6470a5964ec54904 shows zero 'antrieb'-labeled rules), indicating they were cleaned up. All of these were bounded, low-risk, and left no residue in the final state. No unnecessary destructive actions, abandoned files, or exposed insecure configuration were observed in the after-executor snapshot.
